turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
I would prioritize **c030, c038, c097, c088, and c044**. These have the strongest combination of high-efficiency training analogues and physically plausible selective contacts. This is a predicted ranking: the supplied descriptors do not specify thicknesses, surface treatments, or annealing conditions, so they cannot uniquely determine efficiency.

| Rank | Candidate | Training-data and device-physics rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **c030** | The closely matching **PCBM-60 / Bphen, PTAA / PMMA, Al** configuration reaches **19.48%** in training. PTAA provides hole selectivity, while an appropriately thin PMMA modification can suppress interfacial recombination. PCBM/Bphen supports electron extraction and separates the absorber from Al. Adding IDTT2FPDI could improve electron-side coverage or passivation, although that benefit is an extrapolation rather than a measured effect here. |
| **2** | **c038** | The training configuration with **PCBM-60, Au-np / NiO-c, Ag** reaches **20.0%**. c038 retains that hole-side interface and adds PEI after PCBM. A sufficiently thin PEI layer can modify the electron-contact dipole and reduce extraction losses. The strongest evidence is the close 20.0% analogue—not an assumption that Au nanoparticles necessarily improve every device. |
| **3** | **c097** | Its sulfur-containing analogue, **ITCPTC-Th / C60 / BCP, P3CT-Na, Ag**, achieves **18.49%**. The fullerene/BCP stack offers electron selectivity and metal-contact separation, while P3CT-Na is supported by several relatively efficient training recipes. The selenium substitution makes this a promising close analogue, but does not by itself guarantee better performance. |
| **4** | **c088** | **C60 / BCP with PTAA and Cu** is a particularly strong family: training examples reach **18.62%** with sequential spin coating and **19.085%** with slot-die coating. Doctor blading also works well with the same transport layers and Ag (**16.9%**). Willow glass avoids the polymer-substrate processing constraints of PET, making a high-quality coated film plausible. |
| **5** | **c044** | This combines the well-supported **PCBM-60 / BCP–PTAA** selective-contact pair with Cu. The corresponding Ag device reaches **17.345%**, while the closely related **PCBM-60 / C60 / BCP–PTAA–Cu** device reaches **18.85%**. Its simpler electron stack may provide less complete coverage than that triple-layer analogue, but it remains a strong candidate. |

The common advantage is **selectivity at both absorber interfaces plus an electron-contact buffer**, rather than any single material being universally superior. I would not transfer the isolated **24.8% TmPyPB** training result to candidates using other electron-contact modifiers.

**Final: c030, c038, c097, c088, c044**
